## Folio CLI

Folio is a command-line tool for managing notes and indexes. It requires Python 3.11.

### Example Usage

To build a local index from a directory of notes, run the following command:

```bash
folio index ./notes
```

This command will create a local index file in the same directory as your notes. Folio will automatically generate a filename based on the current date and time, ensuring that your index is up-to-date and unique.

### Explanation

- **`folio`:** This is the command name, used to run the Folio tool.
- **`index`:** This is the subcommand, which specifies the action to perform.
- **`./notes`:** This is the path to the directory containing your notes. The `./` symbol indicates the current directory, and `notes` is the name of the directory.
- **`builds`:** This is the behavior of the command, indicating that it will create a local index. In this case, the index is built locally, meaning it will not be uploaded to a remote server.

By using this command, you can easily manage and organize your notes locally, ensuring that your index is always up-to-date and unique.

# Folio CLI Documentation

## Overview

The Folio CLI is a tool used to manage and organize notes and other documents. It provides commands to create, update, and delete notes, as well as to index and search through the indexed notes.

## Examples

### Create a Note

To create a note, use the `note create` command followed by the title and content of the note:

```bash
folio note create "My First Note" "This is my first note."
```

### Update an Existing Note

To update an existing note, use the `note update` command followed by the ID of the note and the new title and content:

```bash
folio note update 1 "My Updated Note" "This is my updated note."
```

### Delete a Note

To delete a note, use the `note delete` command followed by the ID of the note:

```bash
folio note delete 1
```

### Indexing

To build a local index of the notes, use the `folio index ./notes` command:

```bash
folio index ./notes
```

This will create a local index of the notes in the `./notes` directory.

### Searching

To search for notes, use the `folio search` command followed by the search query:

```bash
folio search "My First Note"
```

This will search for notes that contain the phrase "My First Note".
